{"id":"mimid-1wgh.37.108","title":"Write draft-atwood-mimi-calls: media keys for a MIMI-backed call","description":"Step 3 of decision mimid-1wgh.109, and the one that takes real work.
Shaped like draft-atwood-mimi-provider-auth: its own document, with a
replacement-text section for the WG draft it affects.

WHAT IT SAYS, from the worked analysis on bead mimid-96tt:

A call bound to a MIMI room derives its media keys from that room's MLS
group with draft-ietf-mls-extensions §4.4's safe exporter, under a MIMI
media app component.

The load-bearing argument, which the draft has to make plainly because
it decides the shape: §4.4's SafeExportSecret takes a ComponentID and
nothing else and is derived from the epoch secret, so every group member
can compute it. Entitlement cannot be fixed by derivation. Therefore the
group must BE the entitled set, which means a call gets its own room --
room-policy §5's fixed_membership plus parent_dependent. That is not an
incidental example in room-policy; it is the only shape in which the
exporter is the right tool.

What falls out, and should be stated as the payoff: removing someone
from the call is an MLS Remove, which changes the epoch and so the
exported secret, so they lose media access at once and no media-layer
rekey protocol is needed. Adding someone rekeys the same way, so a late
joiner cannot read earlier media.

The subset alternative belongs in the document too, as the case for an
ad-hoc call in an existing room: §4.2's SafeEncryptWithLabel to each
participant's leaf HPKE key. Say its cost -- removing a participant
needs a new key distributed to the remainder, which is the rekey
protocol the first shape avoids -- so an implementer can see why the
first is preferred.

SECTIONS IT NEEDS:
- the component id, provisional and marked as such, with an IANA
  section requesting one from mimi-protocol's app component registry;
- where our responsibility stops: one secret per epoch per component of
  a stated length, and the media layer's own key schedule beyond that
  (SFrame has one);
- rekeying: nothing to specify in the first shape, because the epoch is
  the rekey. Say so, since it is the point;
- security considerations: the entitlement argument above, and what a
  room member who is not on the call can and cannot do;
- replacement text for mimi-content §5.10, in provider-auth's style,
  for whatever §5.10 should say once calling is in scope.

BLOCKED ON NOTHING, but worth waiting on two answers:
- draft-ietf-mimi-content#96, posted 2026-11-23, which asks whether a
  media component is intended at all. A reply saying "out of scope"
  changes this document's framing from a proposal to the WG into an
  extension draft of Mark's own.
- mimi-room-policy#59, posted 2026-11-23, since the first shape cannot
  be implemented while §5 forbids a call containing the whole parent
  set.

Neither blocks writing. {"notes":"WRITTEN AND PUSHED 2026-11-23, Mark's OK:
https://github.com/MarkAtwood/ietf-mimi-calls, commit d997c09,
draft-atwood-mimi-calls-00, 301 lines of kramdown.

Follows the house convention exactly: its own public repo named
ietf-<topic>, holding draft-atwood-mimi-calls.md, the built
draft-atwood-mimi-calls-00.xml and a README, with main as the default
branch, as ietf-mimi-provider-auth and mls-didwebvh-credential do.

SECTIONS: Introduction; Conventions; §3 Why the Group Secret Is Not
Always the Call Secret; §4 A Call in Its Own Room (the room, the
media_keys component, deriving media_secret, rekeying); §5 A Call Among
a Subset of a Room; §6 Security Considerations; §7 IANA; §8 Replacement
Text for MIMI Content; §9 Implementation Status.

§3 is the load-bearing section and says the thing the pieces do not say
for themselves: SafeExportSecret takes a ComponentID and nothing else
and descends from the epoch secret, so every group member can compute
it, so entitlement cannot come from derivation. The twenty-person-room
example is in it, with the point that no protocol error occurs.

§4.4 states the payoff as two bullets: a removed participant loses
subsequent media in the Commit that removed them, and a late joiner
cannot compute an earlier epoch's secret -- so no media-layer rekeying
protocol is needed.

§5 describes the subset case with §4.2's Safe HPKE rather than
forbidding it, and states its cost, so an implementer can see why the
first shape is preferred.

§8 carries replacement text for mimi-content §5.10 in provider-auth's
style, so the draft brings its own patch for the document it affects.

§9 says plainly that mimid implements neither the §4.4 exporter nor
parent-dependent rooms, so nothing here is tested between two
implementations and no interoperability claim is made. That is honest
and it also names the two beads that would change it: mimid-1wgh.4.82
and mimid-1wgh.108.

A note in §4.1 flags the room-policy-04 strict-subset problem and says
the document assumes the rule is a subset, which is what PR
mimi-room-policy#59 asks for.

NOT SUBMITTED to the datatracker and not announced. Both need Mark's own
OK, as every upstream post does. Renders through kramdown-rfc2629 and
xml2rfc with no unresolved references; typos clean."}
